rows.name: Qur'an
rows.detail: Explicit: 'qard hasan' appears in six verses, always a loan 'to Allah'; 2:282 governs recording debts.
rows.detail_long: The goodly-loan phrase runs through 2:245, 5:12, 57:11, 57:18, 64:17 and 73:20 — spending framed as a loan God repays manifold — while 2:282 commands writing debts down.

rows.name: Sahih Bukhari 2068
rows.detail: The Prophet borrowed on credit against his pledged armor — borrowing itself as prophetic practice.
rows.detail_long: The same Aisha narration that anchors rahn shows the Prophet as borrower: credit taken, security given, debt honored. App grading Sahih.

rows.name: Sunan Ibn Majah 2430
rows.detail: 'No Muslim lends to another Muslim twice but it counts as charity once' — graded Da'eef in the app.
rows.detail_long: The lending-virtue narration via Ibn Mas'ud (the Sulaiman bin Udhunan story). The app's own grading is Da'eef — kept as ethics support, not legal proof. Note: the popular short form 'every loan is charity' belongs to a separate al-Tabarani narration outside the app's corpus.

rows.name: Bulugh al-Maram 1024
rows.detail: Guaranteed loan vs borrowed object. 'Is it a loan with a guarantee of return, or a borrowed object to be returned?' — the Prophet distinguishes the two liabilities by name.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: asked for thirty coats of armor, Ya'la asks whether they are a guaranteed loan (madmunah) or a borrowed object ('ariyah) to be returned; the Prophet answers: a borrowed object that must be returned. The earliest-corpus articulation that LOAN and LENT-OBJECT are distinct liability types — the conceptual boundary classical qard doctrine builds on.
rows.evidence_display: Bulugh al-Maram 1024 (text + dating block in app)
rows.internal_ref: Record + dating block read verbatim from app file bulugh-al-maram.json (batch1_source_extract2.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: Ibn Abbas (attrib., Tanwir al-Miqbas)
rows.detail: The earliest attributed gloss on 2:245: the 'goodly loan' as sincere charity, revealed about Abu'l-Dahdah of the Ansar.
rows.detail_long: Tanwir al-Miqbas (in the app) on 2:245: lending to Allah = giving 'in charity sincerely wanting nothing but the sake of Allah', rewarded 'a thousand times', with the revelation-occasion naming Abu'l-Dahdah of the Helpers. The word qard enters the tradition wearing its benevolence meaning first. Attribution traditional, not critical — hence 'attrib.'
rows.evidence_display: Tanwir al-Miqbas (attrib. Ibn Abbas), on Q2:245 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim from app file en-tafsir-ibn-abbas/surah-002.json (batch1_source_extract2.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: Ibn Kathir
rows.detail: Ibn Kathir on 57:11 and 64:17: the loan 'to Allah' as charitable spending with guaranteed manifold repayment.
rows.detail_long: Ibn Kathir's treatments of 57:11 (14,000 chars) and 64:17 (6,600 chars) in the app read the 'goodly loan to Allah' as charitable spending repaid manifold — with the narrations of Ibn Mas'ud and Abu'd-Dahdah giving his garden against a date-palm in Paradise. The theological frame that makes interest-free lending worship.
rows.evidence_display: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, on Q57:11 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim this session from app tafsir file (batch2_source_extract.json)

rows.name: Mufti Muhammad Shafi Usmani
rows.detail: Ma'ariful Qur'an on 2:245: the 'loan to Allah' is figurative — AND real lending to His slaves in their hour of need is itself credited with great merit.
rows.detail_long: The app's Ma'ariful Qur'an passage on 2:245 (read this session): 'loan' figuratively means spending in Allah's way, surely returned like a loan — a date given grows past Mount Uhud — and the verse has ALSO been read as actual lending to human beings, 'thereby helping them in their hour of need... credited with great merit in Hadith'. The modern mufassir holding both readings together: charity AND the interest-free loan. NOTE: figure upgraded from finance-local to app slug F2020 this session.
rows.evidence_display: Ma'ariful Qur'an, on Q2:245 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim from app file en-tafsir-maarif-ul-quran/surah-002.json (batch1_source_extract2.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: Classical consensus (four schools)
rows.work_title: Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali fiqh manuals
rows.detail: Universal from the earliest fiqh: qard is gratuitous; ANY stipulated increase is riba; repay exactly the principal.
rows.detail_long: No school ever wavered: the loan contract admits no stipulated benefit to the lender — the bright line that makes qard the anti-interest contract. Year set at 795 (earliest surviving school literature, Malik's Muwatta) as the recording point.
rows.evidence_display: Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali fiqh manuals

rows.timeline_year_basis: adopted Shari'ah Board meeting 12, Al-Madinah, 26-30 Rabi' I 1425 / 15-19 May 2004
rows.name: AAOIFI
rows.detail: AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 19 (Qard), adopted 2004: microfinance, current accounts; voluntary extra repayment allowed if unstipulated.
rows.detail_long: SS19 keeps the classical rule and adds banking detail. VERIFIED adoption 19 May 2004. CLAUSES VERIFIED-TO-TEXT (ss1.txt, earlier session per quran_finance_layer v2): 4/1 stipulated excess = riba in any form (quality, quantity, benefit, written or customary); 5/2 voluntary excess at repayment permissible if not stipulated or customary; 7 no tying a sale or lease to the qard; 9/1-9/2 service charges limited to actual direct costs, method set by the Shari'ah Supervisory Board, indirect costs excluded; 10/1/1 current accounts are loans.
rows.internal_ref: Adoption verified earlier session; clause set carried from quran_finance_layer.json v2 worked chain (SS19 clauses verified-to-text)

rows.name: Industry practice
rows.detail: Qard hasan runs current accounts, microfinance and benevolent funds.
rows.detail_long: Islamic current accounts are legally interest-free loans to the bank; qard-hasan funds anchor Islamic microfinance and student/hardship lending.
